title: Mixed-workload scheduler: raw benchmark results (runtime-1.18 candidate)
content:
Doc purpose
- Raw capture of benchmark runs for mixed-workload scheduler prototype.
- Includes: run logs, parameter sweeps, tables (p50/p95/throughput), and links to dashboards.
- NOT a polished summary (see Confluence results write-up). This is the scratchpad / export we used to generate summary charts.

Last updated: 2026-02-02 (RK)

=====
Test matrix (high level)

Runtime builds
- Baseline: runtime-1.17.6 (prod-ish)
- Candidate: runtime-1.18.0-rc3 (includes short/long classification + two-queue + token budgets + per-class metrics)

Models
- llama-3.1-70b-instruct (tp=8)  [primary]
- llama-3.1-8b-instruct (tp=2)    [sanity / sensitivity]

SKUs
- aws p4de (A100 80GB x8)   label: A100x8
- aws p5 (H100 80GB x8)     label: H100x8
- gcp a2-ultragpu (A100 80GB x8) label: A100x8-gcp (limited runs)

Regions
- us-east-1 (primary)
- eu-west-1 (spot-check)

Scenarios (benchmark-lab PR-903)
- MIX_80_20: 80% short prompts + 20% long-context prompts
- MIX_50_50: balanced
- LONG_SPIKE: steady 80/20 then inject 60s burst of long requests (prefill-heavy)

Prompt distributions (generator settings)
- SHORT: prompt_tokens ~ [16..256], target_new_tokens=128 (p50 ~ 96)
- LONG: prompt_tokens ~ [2048..8192], target_new_tokens=128 (prefill dominates)
- Concurrency: 64 clients unless noted
- Request rate: closed-loop (clients issue next request after prior completes)

Success lens (not enforced here, just recorded)
- Reduce user-visible p95 E2E latency + p95 TTFT for short class under mix, while holding throughput within ~0-5% of baseline.

=====
Scheduler policy knobs under test

Common
- enable_mixed_scheduler: true|false
- classify_by: prompt_tokens (fixed for these runs)
- short_threshold_tokens: {256, 384, 512}

Two-queue dispatch
- short_queue_weight (dispatch share target): {0.60, 0.70, 0.80}
- aging_half_life_ms (long-queue aging boost): {2500, 5000, 10000}
- max_short_burst_iters: {8, 16}

Token budgets (per scheduling iteration)
- token_budget_short: {4096, 6144}
- token_budget_long: {2048, 3072}

Notes
- Some runs include “prefill/decode separation hooks” on by default in rc3.
- Kernel selection stability was monitored via “kernel_variant_switches/sec” metric; we annotated any >3/sec as “thrash risk”.

=====
Command template / run protocol

Benchmark-lab invocation (example)
- benchlab run \
    --scenario MIX_80_20 \
    --model llama-3.1-70b-instruct \
    --region us-east-1 \
    --sku H100x8 \
    --runtime runtime-1.18.0-rc3 \
    --duration 900 \
    --warmup 120 \
    --clients 64 \
    --scheduler.enable_mixed_scheduler=true \
    --scheduler.short_threshold_tokens=384 \
    --scheduler.short_queue_weight=0.70 \
    --scheduler.aging_half_life_ms=5000 \
    --scheduler.token_budget_short=6144 \
    --scheduler.token_budget_long=3072

Protocol
- Warmup: first 120s ignored
- Collect: next 780s
- 3 repetitions per config unless otherwise noted
- Metrics captured
  - E2E latency (ms): p50/p95/p99
  - TTFT (ms): p50/p95/p99
  - Throughput: output_tokens/s (server) + req/s
  - Queue time (ms): p50/p95 (overall + per-class when enabled)
  - GPU util (%), KV cache hit (%), batch size stats

Grafana dashboards used (links)
- Scheduler class metrics
  https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/sched-class/scheduler-class-metrics?var-region=us-east-1&var-sku=H100x8
- Runtime latency/throughput overview
  https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/runtime-ov/runtime-overview?var-region=us-east-1&var-model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Kernel variant stability
  https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kern-stab/kernel-stability?var-region=us-east-1

Perf-canary job
- Mixed workload nightly: https://perf-canary.redwood.internal/jobs/mixed_workload_scheduler_nightly

Cfg shorthand decoding
- S{N} = short_threshold_tokens N
- W{X} = short_queue_weight X% (0.70 => 70%)
- A{M} = aging_half_life_ms (A5 => 5000ms, A10 => 10000ms, A2.5 => 2500ms)
- T{short}/{long} = token_budget_short (k) / token_budget_long (k) per iter
  - T6/3 => 6144/3072
  - T4/2 => 4096/2048

=====
RAW LOG SNIPPETS / ANNOTATIONS

(1) MW-118-003 kernel switching spike
- Observed on W80 + long budget 2048 (T6/2). Grafana kernel stability panel shows variant switches ~3-5/sec during mixed prefill/decode.
- Snippet from runtime log (redacted)
  2026-01-12T22:14:31.220Z [sched] class=short dispatch batch=12 prefill=2 decode=10 token_budget_short=6144
  2026-01-12T22:14:31.228Z [kern] select variant=flashattn_v3 seq=128
  2026-01-12T22:14:31.244Z [kern] select variant=triton_prefill_chunked seq=6144
  2026-01-12T22:14:31.261Z [kern] select variant=flashattn_v3 seq=128
  2026-01-12T22:14:31.277Z [kern] select variant=triton_prefill_chunked seq=6144
- Operator note: weight=0.80 caused more frequent alternating short/long micro-batches.

(2) MW-118-008 eu-west-1 packet loss
- Single 8s period of elevated request error/timeout from client runner.
- Marked in benchlab as “infra noise”; metrics window excluded around t=420..450.

=====
Open items / follow-ups (from this sheet)
- Re-run A100x8 MIX_80_20 with S384_W70_A10_T4/2 (we only have S512 threshold run as “official”).
- Investigate kernel thrash mitigation for W80 configs (maybe min-run-length per class, or clamp prefill chunk size selection under high alternation).
- Confirm starvation counter semantics with Julian (does it count “aging emergency dispatch” only, or also “max wait exceeded”?)
- Perf-canary: add alert for kernel_switches_per_s >3 sustained for 5m on mixed workloads (Sahana + Allison).
